topics.name: Execution Context
topics.notes:
if variable x is nowhere in the code, 
console.log(x) => ReferenceError: x is not defined
but, console.log(window.x) => undefined 

this is because the first log looks for variable, that does not exist. but in the second case, window is a global object. 
if you try to access a property of an object and it doesn't exist, js returns undefined.

topics.name: Scope
topics.notes:
- Variable shadowing happens when a variable declared in an inner scope has the same name as a variable in an outer scope.
- Root-level let/const are stored in the global lexical environment, which Chrome labels as Script. Root-level var and function declarations become properties of the global object, which Chrome labels as Global. When execution enters the block, JavaScript creates a new lexical environment, which Chrome labels as Block.

dsaProblems.name: Valid anagram
dsaProblems.notes:
Brute force:
- count the no.of times each char occurs
- compare if it's the same count for both words

Optimised:
- You can count characters from s, then subtract while traversing t.
- One hash map instead of two. Less memory. Still O(n) time.
Interviewers generally like this because it shows you recognize that you only need to track the difference in frequencies, not two complete frequency tables.
